title: KadaVerse 30-Day Social Prompt Book
description: A 30-day, product-aware social campaign prompt book. Import it into Marketing → Social Studio. All imported entries become drafts.

posts.title: KadaVerse studio introduction
posts.audience: business owners and founders
posts.headline: Software that moves business forward.
posts.caption: KadaVerse builds websites and software around the way a business works: customer platforms, mobile apps, and systems for everyday operations. We are based in Kannur and work with businesses across India. What are you trying to make easier in your business?
posts.ctaNote: Start a project at thekada.in/start-project.
posts.visualDirection: A bouquet of three elegant cards for websites, apps, and business systems, held against a light blue/off-white studio background. Use the bouquet composition from Ref 6; use KadaVerse navy and blue, not the reference brand's palette.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show three clear cards, each with one simple original icon and one label: “Websites”, “Apps”, “Business systems”. Keep the cards arranged like a thoughtful selection, not a crowded services list. Place the headline above and the CTA below. Include the supplied KadaVerse wordmark.

posts.title: Web applications
posts.audience: businesses taking enquiries, bookings, or orders
posts.goal: make the value of a business website concrete
posts.headline: Your website should move enquiries forward.
posts.caption: A useful website helps the right person understand what you offer and take the next step. That might be a quote request, booking, order, or structured enquiry. We design the flow around the way your team responds.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us what visitors should be able to do.
posts.visualDirection: A real browser page presented on a clean floating card, with one clear enquiry action visible. Use the offer-card composition from Ref 4 without copying its free-preview offer.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a refined, bright poster with a large browser-card mock-up showing an approved KadaVerse or client website screen. If no approved screen is attached, use a restrained generic layout with no readable fake company names. Headline at the top, three short service labels nearby, CTA at the bottom.

posts.title: The Kada
posts.audience: local consumers in supported service areas
posts.headline: Order, dine and stay — one local app.
posts.support: Explore food, tables, and stays nearby
posts.caption: The Kada brings local restaurants, dining, and stays into one app. Check availability for your area, browse what is nearby, and follow your order on the map when you choose delivery.
posts.ctaNote: Visit order.thekada.in or check the app in your area.
posts.visualDirection: One real phone screen in a warm everyday Kerala setting, with a few food and stay cues around it. Use the contextual product-screen idea from Ref 3 and the device focus from Ref 17.
posts.dailyPrompt: Use the supplied The Kada screen in a realistic hand-held phone. Keep the interface unchanged. Create a calm local-food scene with natural light and a subtle map/route motif. Use The Kada blue accent and exact app name. Do not invent restaurant listings, offers, or availability claims.

posts.title: Kada Dine
posts.audience: restaurant owners and managers
posts.goal: show the product as an operations system
posts.headline: One POS for the floor and kitchen.
posts.caption: Kada Dine connects counter billing, QR table ordering, and kitchen tickets in one restaurant system. It also supports inventory, staff, and reporting for food businesses.
posts.ctaNote: Explore the Kada Dine product page.
posts.visualDirection: A confident POS-device hero with the real Kada Dine interface. Use the product-device composition from Ref 13.
posts.dailyPrompt: Place a tablet or POS terminal at the center of a clean restaurant counter scene. Show only the supplied Kada Dine screen. Add three small floating feature labels: “Billing”, “QR ordering”, “Kitchen display”. Use Kada Dine's orange accent sparingly within the KadaVerse navy/cream system. Do not add sales figures.

posts.title: SellrApp
posts.audience: small retailers and social sellers
posts.headline: Your store link. Your brand. Your orders.
posts.support: A storefront built for independent sellers
posts.caption: SellrApp gives a seller a branded storefront and a place to manage products and orders. Orders from the store, WhatsApp, or the counter can be followed from one list.
posts.ctaNote: Visit sellrapp.vercel.app.
posts.visualDirection: A storefront card emerging from a phone with a few product tiles. Use the clean app-launch layouts from Ref 18 or 19; retain SellrApp's amber accent.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show a phone beside a floating branded storefront card using the supplied SellrApp screens. Keep products generic unless real approved product imagery is provided. Use exact poster copy only, with amber as a small accent. No fake sales or conversion metrics.

posts.title: Kada Stay
posts.audience: hotels, homestays, hostels, and guests
posts.headline: Bookings and guest service, together.
posts.support: For stays, rooms, and guest requests
posts.caption: Kada Stay connects property listings and direct bookings with tools for the people running the property. The host app supports front-desk work, room status, guest messaging, and service requests.
posts.ctaNote: Explore Kada Stay on the KadaVerse website.
posts.visualDirection: A host holding a room or booking card, paired with a real host-app screen. Use the calendar/held-screen idea from Ref 3.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a welcoming hospitality scene with a property host holding a clean booking panel. Use an attached real Kada Stay screen for the phone or tablet UI. Keep the scene specific to a modest, contemporary Kerala stay; avoid luxury claims or invented property brands.

posts.title: How a software project starts
posts.audience: businesses considering custom software
posts.headline: First understand the work. Then build.
posts.caption: We begin by understanding the users, the current process, and the first useful outcome. Then we agree on scope, milestones, and what the team will review at each step.
posts.ctaNote: Bring us the workflow that feels stuck.
posts.visualDirection: A four-piece puzzle representing discovery, scope, design, and demo. Use Ref 12's puzzle structure, with clean labels.
posts.dailyPrompt: Build one connected four-piece process diagram. Label the pieces exactly “Discover”, “Scope”, “Design”, and “Demo”. Use navy outlines, blue highlights, and generous white space. Keep the iconography simple and avoid implying a guaranteed launch date.

posts.title: Kada Delivery
posts.audience: prospective riders and fleet partners
posts.headline: A clearer handoff for every delivery.
posts.caption: Kada Delivery is the rider and dispatch side of The Kada. Riders can receive zone-based offers, navigate pickup and drop, confirm handover with a customer code, and review their earnings record.
posts.ctaNote: Apply at partner.thekada.in/join. App access follows approval and onboarding.
posts.visualDirection: Rider phone plus four feature cards arranged around it. Use Ref 14's feature layout and Ref 16's field-team product composition.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show a delivery rider beside a phone using the supplied real rider screen. Add three small feature tiles labelled “Zone-based offers”, “Navigation”, and “Verified handover”. Use Kada Delivery's cyan accent as a detail. Do not promise a particular earning amount or guaranteed work.

posts.title: Automation and AI
posts.audience: teams repeating the same admin tasks
posts.headline: Let repeat work follow a clearer path.
posts.caption: Automation is most useful when it removes a repeated handoff or helps people find the information they need. We map the process first, then identify where automation or AI fits.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us about one task your team repeats.
posts.visualDirection: A calm visual metaphor: scattered message and document cards flowing into one simple connected path. Use Ref 8's workload metaphor or a single oversized translucent key from Ref 27 to suggest control. Avoid fake alert counts and claims that everything can be automated.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a before-and-after flow: a few neutral request cards enter a clean sequence of steps, then arrive at one organised work queue. Use no readable personal data, company logos, or AI robot character. Keep the message grounded and practical.

posts.title: Kada Mess
posts.audience: mess kitchens, PG/hostel kitchens, and office canteens
posts.headline: Monthly meal plans. Clear headcounts.
posts.caption: Kada Mess is being prepared for launch with kitchen partners. It is designed around monthly meal plans, weekly menus, and a cut-off for each meal so a kitchen can see its planned headcount.
posts.ctaNote: If you run a mess kitchen, contact us to discuss the early group.
posts.visualDirection: A weekly meal calendar connected to a kitchen planning screen. Use Ref 3's calendar motif and Ref 7's collaborative board.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show a clean weekly menu card beside a real or approved Kada Mess screen. Add a visible “In development” label and a small “Join the early list” CTA. Do not show fabricated subscriber counts, prices, or launch dates.

posts.title: UI/UX and MVP design
posts.audience: founders and teams with an early product idea
posts.goal: encourage testing the idea before a full build
posts.headline: Make the first version clear before the build.
posts.support: User flows · Interface design · Clickable prototypes
posts.caption: A clickable prototype can help a team discuss the user journey and the first version before engineering begins. We map the key screens and decisions so the scope has something concrete to respond to.
posts.ctaNote: Share the idea you want to make testable.
posts.visualDirection: Layered prototype screens held together by one clear flow. Use Ref 17's layered-screen treatment and Ref 12's step-by-step idea.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a polished set of three overlapping app prototype screens connected by a thin blue path. Keep interface text minimal and legible; use no fabricated live metrics. Add a small “Clickable prototype” label, with the headline as the focal point.

posts.title: Kada Ledger
posts.audience: shops and service businesses that track credit
posts.goal: introduce the digital khata and invite early-access enquiries
posts.headline: Every balance, out of the paper book.
posts.support: Record credit · See balances · Share on WhatsApp
posts.caption: Kada Ledger is a digital khata for businesses that record customer credit. It keeps balances and payment history together, and can prepare a balance message to share through WhatsApp.
posts.ctaNote: Join the early-access group through the KadaVerse contact page.
posts.visualDirection: A paper ledger page dissolving into a phone displaying the real Kada Ledger screen. Use a single bright green accent and an uncluttered light background.
posts.dailyPrompt: Compose a simple paper-to-phone transition. Use the supplied Kada Ledger product screen and logo. Include “Early access” clearly. Do not show real customer names, balances, or financial records; use approved demo data only.

posts.title: Raman Caterings case
posts.audience: caterers and service businesses managing custom enquiries
posts.headline: From event enquiry to clear quotation.
posts.support: Website form → team inbox → quote for review
posts.caption: For Raman Caterings, the project includes a mobile-first website, a structured event enquiry form, a staff inbox, and custom quotations customers can review online. The post describes the system built; it makes no claim about measured sales or enquiry growth.
posts.ctaNote: Ask us about a similar enquiry-to-quote workflow.
posts.visualDirection: Three connected panels showing the real website, staff inbox, and quote review screen. Client name, logo, and screens require approval before publication.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a three-stage horizontal-to-vertical flow using only client-approved Raman Caterings screens and branding. If approval or screens are missing, use anonymised generic panels and remove the client name. Add no metrics or testimonials.

posts.title: Cloud and DevOps
posts.audience: businesses with a live app or website
posts.goal: explain the foundation behind reliable releases
posts.headline: A steadier home for your product.
posts.caption: Cloud and DevOps work covers the parts people may not see in a product demo: deployment paths, monitoring, backups, and the setup a team uses to ship changes.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us what you run today and what feels hard to maintain.
posts.visualDirection: A layered cloud system with a small release path and backup symbol. Keep it clear and human rather than a dense infrastructure diagram.
posts.dailyPrompt: Illustrate a product sitting on a stable cloud foundation, with three simple labels: “Deploys”, “Monitoring”, “Backups”. Use a restrained blue glow against navy/cream. Do not include uptime percentages, certifications, or security guarantees.

posts.title: Kada Stay host operations
posts.audience: hostel, PG, and multi-room property operators
posts.goal: show a property management use case
posts.headline: Rooms, residents, and rent in one view.
posts.support: Host tools for stays and long-term rooms
posts.caption: Kada Stay includes host tools for rooms and beds, residents, rent, front-desk activity, and housekeeping. It also supports guest services for hotels and homestays.
posts.ctaNote: See whether the host workflow fits your property.
posts.visualDirection: A calm floor-plan or room grid beside the actual host app, with one highlighted room status. Use Ref 16's field-and-screen pairing.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a property operations poster with a simple room/bed grid and one phone showing the supplied Kada Stay host screen. Use blue and neutral hospitality tones. Avoid inventing occupancy rates, tenant details, or property names.

posts.title: API integrations
posts.audience: businesses using disconnected tools
posts.headline: Connect the tools your business already uses.
posts.caption: When a payment, message, or update needs to be copied between tools, an integration can keep that handoff in one flow. We first confirm the systems and data involved, then scope the connection.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us which tools need to share information.
posts.visualDirection: Four labeled tiles connected by a single route. Use the modular card language from Ref 5 or the puzzle logic in Ref 12.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show four simple nodes labelled “Payments”, “Maps”, “Messages”, and “Business data”, connected through one clear central system. Use no third-party logos unless specifically supplied and approved. Avoid suggesting every tool is already integrated.

posts.title: Mobile app development
posts.audience: founders and businesses considering an app
posts.goal: show app development as a user-centered service
posts.headline: Build the app around the person using it.
posts.caption: The right app begins with the user and the task. KadaVerse designs and builds mobile experiences for customers and teams, including payments, maps, notifications, and other device features when the product needs them.
posts.ctaNote: Start with the first user journey you need to support.
posts.visualDirection: One central phone surrounded by four small capability cards. Use Ref 15's app-service composition and Ref 17's layered screens.
posts.dailyPrompt: Place one phone with an approved KadaVerse product screen at the center. Arrange four clean cards around it labelled “User flow”, “Payments”, “Maps”, and “Notifications”. Keep the app content truthful and avoid promises of engagement or revenue growth.

posts.title: KadaVerse capability overview
posts.audience: business decision-makers
posts.goal: show the breadth of the studio at a glance
posts.headline: Nine service areas. One product team.
posts.support: Web · Mobile · SaaS · Business systems · AI · Marketing · Design · Cloud · Integrations
posts.caption: KadaVerse works across nine areas, from web and mobile products to business systems, design, cloud, and integrations. We can help define a focused first release or support a wider product roadmap.
posts.ctaNote: Explore the services at thekada.in/services.
posts.visualDirection: A top-down planning table with nine tidy capability cards and one central KadaVerse mark. Use Ref 7's collaborative tabletop layout and Ref 20's count-led hierarchy. The number nine is the count of the current website service areas, not a performance claim.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a top-down studio table with nine readable service cards arranged around one central blue card labelled “KadaVerse”. Use only the exact service labels listed in the support line. Keep spacing generous and avoid extra microcopy.

posts.title: The Kada local discovery
posts.audience: consumers looking for nearby food and stays
posts.headline: Find your next local favourite.
posts.caption: The Kada helps customers browse local restaurants and cafés, book a table, and find stays. Service availability depends on location, so check the app or website for your area.
posts.ctaNote: Visit order.thekada.in.
posts.visualDirection: A phone with the real discovery screen over a subtle map-like background. Use the search-bar idea in Ref 9 and the contextual phone treatment in Ref 3.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show a clean phone with the supplied The Kada browse screen. Add a restrained location pin and soft map contours behind it. Do not invent neighborhood names, restaurant listings, discounts, or coverage claims.

posts.title: Kada Dine AI menu import
posts.audience: restaurant owners and managers
posts.headline: A printed menu becomes a digital draft.
posts.support: Review the dishes and prices before publishing
posts.caption: Kada Dine can read a photo or PDF of a printed menu and create a draft digital menu for the restaurant team to review and edit before it is used.
posts.ctaNote: Explore Kada Dine at kadadine.thekada.in.
posts.visualDirection: Printed menu on one side, phone showing an approved editable digital-menu screen on the other. Use the product showcase style of Ref 13.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a clean transformation scene from a paper menu to a digital menu draft on a tablet. Use the supplied Kada Dine screen if available; otherwise leave the screen clean for real UI placement. Make the review/edit step visible. Do not imply a menu publishes without human review.

posts.title: Digital marketing
posts.audience: businesses seeking clearer online discovery and enquiries
posts.goal: position marketing around a measurable next step
posts.headline: Make the next step easy to find.
posts.support: Local search · Ads · Landing pages · Tracking
posts.caption: Digital marketing should connect discovery to an action a business can understand, such as a call, booking, or enquiry. KadaVerse works across local search, Google and Meta ads, landing pages, and tracking.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us what action you want customers to take.
posts.visualDirection: A search or ad card leads into a focused landing page and an enquiry action. Use the large search concept in Ref 9 and, if a warning-style composition fits, the broken-key metaphor from Ref 31 to signal planning before spend. Do not use fear-based copy.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a simple three-step visual: “Discover”, “Understand”, “Enquire”. Use a search card, a clean landing-page preview, and one clear CTA tile. Use no platform logos or performance metrics. Keep the headline as the dominant text.

posts.title: SellrApp order management
posts.audience: retailers and social sellers already taking orders in multiple places
posts.headline: One order list for store and WhatsApp.
posts.support: Add counter orders to the same view
posts.caption: SellrApp brings orders from the online store, WhatsApp, and the counter into one dashboard. It also supports product catalogues, coupons, reviews, and customer records.
posts.ctaNote: Visit sellrapp.vercel.app.
posts.visualDirection: Three incoming order cards converge into one store dashboard. Use the service-board idea from Ref 5 or the product-card language from Ref 7.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show three clean source cards labelled “Store”, “WhatsApp”, and “Counter” flowing into one supplied SellrApp order screen. Keep sample order data generic. Use amber only as a detail; do not make sales claims.

posts.title: Kada Delivery rider features
posts.audience: riders and fleet operators
posts.goal: explain the rider experience with feature proof
posts.headline: Offer. Navigate. Verify. Reconcile.
posts.support: The rider tools behind The Kada
posts.caption: Kada Delivery supports the rider workflow from an offer through pickup, drop, customer-confirmed handover, and an earnings ledger. Riders are onboarded after an application and review.
posts.ctaNote: Apply at partner.thekada.in/join.
posts.visualDirection: A phone-led feature hero with four small panels orbiting around it. Use Ref 14's device-feature composition and Ref 16's field user.
posts.dailyPrompt: Use the approved Kada Rider screen as the hero. Add four short labels exactly: “Offer”, “Navigate”, “Verify”, “Reconcile”. Show a rider in a grounded local delivery setting. Do not claim guaranteed work or a fixed earning amount.

posts.title: Business software and Task Pilot
posts.audience: construction firms and field teams
posts.goal: demonstrate a custom system for office and field operations
posts.headline: One system for office and site work.
posts.caption: Task Pilot is a web dashboard and mobile app built for Kurickal Developers LLP. The system includes projects, tasks, attendance, site diaries, documents, leave, expenses, and team chat. This post uses product capabilities only; it does not claim a measured productivity result. Publish the client name and screens only after approval.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us where your office and field workflows lose context.
posts.visualDirection: A field worker and manager connected through an approved screen pair. Use Ref 16's field-user layout and Ref 7's coordination-board idea.
posts.dailyPrompt: Pair an approved Task Pilot phone screen with a web dashboard on a clean split composition. If the client has not approved public use, remove the client name and use anonymised demo screens. Show only the listed capabilities and no private records.

posts.title: Kada Verse partner app
posts.audience: people and businesses with local business networks
posts.headline: Know local businesses? Partner with Kada.
posts.support: Register leads and follow onboarding in the partner app
posts.caption: Approved partners can introduce restaurants, stays, kitchens, and other businesses to Kada products and follow their leads in the Kada Verse partner app. Partner terms and commissions are set out in the agreement; earnings are not guaranteed.
posts.ctaNote: Apply at thekada.in/become-a-partner.
posts.visualDirection: A network of local business cards feeding into a clear partner dashboard. Use the bouquet or service-selection style from Ref 6; label the app “Kada Verse partner app” to distinguish it from the KadaVerse studio.
posts.dailyPrompt: Show a simple network of restaurant, stay, and kitchen cards connected to a phone with an approved partner-app screen. Use the exact app label “Kada Verse partner app”. Avoid commission amounts, guaranteed earnings, or claims of instant approval.

posts.title: SaaS product development
posts.audience: founders and companies building a subscription product
posts.headline: Turn your product idea into a usable first release.
posts.caption: Building a SaaS product includes more than the customer-facing screens. The first release may also need account roles, billing, an admin view, and a clear way to learn from usage.
posts.ctaNote: Start by describing the first user and their main task.
posts.visualDirection: A product idea card becomes a small set of connected screens. Use the keyboard-key metaphors from Refs 21–24 or 27–30 to suggest making a product fit its users, or use the process puzzle from Ref 12.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a minimal transformation: one idea card on the left, a connected product flow on the right. Use a subtle keyboard-key motif with the letters “MVP” only if it remains legible. Do not promise user growth, retention, or funding outcomes.

posts.title: Inspiro 26 event platform
posts.audience: event and education organisers
posts.goal: show an event workflow from registration to results
posts.headline: Registration to check-in, one event flow.
posts.caption: The Inspiro 26 event platform supported registrations, payment tracking, QR passes, check-in, event schedules, results, PDF exports, and certificates. The post focuses on the workflow, not on unverified attendance or revenue outcomes.
posts.ctaNote: Tell us what your event team needs to coordinate.
posts.visualDirection: One QR pass links a registration card, check-in screen, and results page. Use the process cards from Ref 12 and the product-screen treatment in Ref 17.
posts.dailyPrompt: Use approved Inspiro 26 screenshots or anonymised demo screens to show “Register → Check in → Publish results”. Keep all personal data out. Remove client name and logo until publication is approved.

posts.title: We run what we build
posts.audience: businesses choosing a development partner
posts.headline: We build and run digital products.
posts.caption: KadaVerse builds products as well as client software. The team works on customer ordering, restaurant operations, stays, and rider workflows, giving us direct experience with the decisions that continue after launch.
posts.ctaNote: Explore the products and project work on the website.
posts.visualDirection: A focused product-screen gallery with four real interfaces; use Ref 17's layered-screen depth. Do not use unverified user counts or results.
posts.dailyPrompt: Arrange four supplied product screens in a clean layered composition, labelled exactly “Ordering”, “Restaurant operations”, “Stays”, and “Delivery”. Keep the original UI intact and use the KadaVerse master palette.

posts.title: The people and process
posts.audience: prospective clients and team members
posts.goal: make the studio feel approachable and accountable
posts.headline: One team from first sketch to handover.
posts.caption: KadaVerse brings design, engineering, launch, and support into one project team. Clients can review working builds and understand the next decision as the product takes shape.
posts.ctaNote: Follow along or tell us what your team is building.
posts.visualDirection: A candid real team/workbench photo or a top-down planning table. Use Ref 7's collaborative composition. Use only real approved team images; otherwise use an object-led desk scene, not invented people.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create a warm, realistic studio planning scene with a laptop, notebook, prototype cards, and a real team photo if supplied. Keep identifiable people out unless approved. Add the supplied KadaVerse wordmark and exact poster copy.

posts.title: Start a project with KadaVerse
posts.audience: qualified business owners and founders
posts.headline: Have a business problem? Let’s shape the first useful version.
posts.support: Free discovery call · Written scope · Clear next step
posts.caption: You do not need a finished specification to start a conversation. Tell us who needs help, what is difficult today, and what a useful first version would let them do. KadaVerse starts with a short discovery call, then prepares a written scope and proposal for projects that are a fit.
posts.ctaNote: Start at thekada.in/start-project.
posts.visualDirection: A clean invitation card over a target or a small connected flow from problem to first version. Use the prominent card treatment from Ref 4 or the goal composition from Ref 32.
posts.dailyPrompt: Create an elegant invitation poster with a large central card. Show a simple three-step line: “Business problem → First version → Project plan”. Keep the free discovery call wording exact. Add no deadline, price, limited-slot claim, or guarantee.
